title: PostGIS Spatial Indexing vs In-Memory Haversine: Sub-12ms Radius Lookups
dilemma: How to query partner service center polygons across Riyadh & Jeddah under high concurrency without CPU throttling or slow table scans.
solution: PostgreSQL PostGIS with GIST R-tree spatial indexing and ST_DWithin queries, dropping lookup P95 from 340ms to 11.4ms.
tradeoff: PostGIS ST_DWithin + GIST Index vs In-memory Haversine filtering on unindexed rows

title: Preventing Wash Bay Double-Booking with Redis Distributed Locks & SELECT FOR UPDATE
dilemma: Concurrent customers selecting the same physical wash bay during peak hours causing double-booking conflicts.
solution: Two-tier locking: atomic Redis distributed lock (SET lock:bay:{id} customer_id NX PX 180000) during checkout followed by PostgreSQL SELECT FOR UPDATE on payment capture.
tradeoff: Redis Atomic Distributed Lock + SELECT FOR UPDATE vs Optimistic timestamp checks with late rollback

title: Idempotent Financial Settlement Ledgers with Celery & ON CONFLICT
dilemma: Worker retries or network failures during automated partner commission splits causing duplicate payout transactions.
solution: Decoupled asynchronous Celery settlement tasks writing to an immutable ledger with unique booking idempotency keys using ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
tradeoff: Celery Worker + Unique Idempotency Ledger Key vs Synchronous HTTP webhooks during checkout

title: Row-Level Multi-Tenancy vs Database-per-Tenant Sprawl Across 40+ Schools
dilemma: Serving 40+ schools across 5 districts: database-per-tenant creates massive DevOps sprawl and connection bloat, while naive shared databases risk catastrophic cross-tenant data leaks.
solution: Single shared PostgreSQL 16 database enforced by strict row-level policy scoping layers on work_stream_id across all 64 relational entities, validated by 665 automated CI tests.
metrics: 64 relational entities, 40+ schools, 665 green CI tests
tradeoff: Shared DB + Strict Service Policy Layer vs Database-per-tenant with high DevOps sprawl

title: Origin-Scoped Subdomain Storage vs Shared Root Cookie Session Bleeding
dilemma: Tenants accessing customized subdomains (*.edutracker.site) risking cross-tenant privilege escalation or token leakage if global root cookies are shared.
solution: Wildcard DNS with host header tenant resolution (P95 < 2.8ms) and origin-scoped sessionStorage JWT storage, strictly enforced by browser origin boundaries.
metrics: Subdomain resolution P95 < 2.8ms, zero cross-tenant leakage
tradeoff: Subdomain DNS + Origin-Scoped Storage vs Global SSO cookies spanning all tenant subdomains

title: Asynchronous Batch PDF Report Card Compilation vs HTTP Gateway Timeouts
dilemma: Compiling hundreds of district-wide student gradebook PDFs at semester end causing 504 Gateway Timeouts and starving web server threads.
solution: Dedicated Celery worker pools with Redis queue segregation, compiling WeasyPrint PDFs in background tasks with exponential backoff retries and WebSocket readiness notifications.
metrics: Zero HTTP gateway timeouts during mass generation
tradeoff: Celery Async Workers + Redis Broker vs Synchronous HTTP request processing

title: Pure-Python Hybrid Search (BM25 + ChromaDB Dense RRF) Eliminating Elasticsearch
dilemma: Dense vector search alone missed exact SKU and order ID lookups, but spinning up Elasticsearch/Meilisearch clusters introduced immense RAM consumption and operational complexity.
solution: In-process pure-Python hybrid search combining ChromaDB dense vector queries with an in-memory BM25 lexical index, fused using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60) and MMR diversity filtering.
tradeoff: ChromaDB Dense + Pure-Python BM25 / RRF vs Dense-only vector search or heavy external Elasticsearch clusters

title: Arabic Text Normalization & Orthographic Folding in Vector Pipelines
dilemma: Arabic queries and corporate documents have huge spelling variations (hamza/alef forms, taa-marbuta, Eastern numerals) resulting in poor semantic and lexical recall.
solution: Lightweight deterministic regex pipeline stripping diacritics, folding alef/yaa variants, and mapping Eastern numerals (٥->5) applied symmetrically to documents and queries.
metrics: Zero false-negative misses due to diacritics or numeral formats
tradeoff: In-line deterministic normalization vs Relying purely on raw LLM tokenizer embeddings

title: Resilient Multi-Provider LLM Failover with Persistent HTTP/2 Connection Pools
dilemma: Proprietary LLM API rate limits, regional outages, or sudden latency spikes crashing customer support channels.
solution: OpenAI-compatible unified interface failing over dynamically: Gemini 3.8/2.5 Flash -> DeepSeek-V3 -> OpenAI GPT-4o-mini, backed by persistent process-cached httpx connection pools.
tradeoff: Ordered Provider Chain + Reusable httpx Pool vs Single Provider SDK with late request crash

title: Closed-Loop Real-Time Knowledge Base Learning from Human Escalation Tickets
dilemma: When AI encounters unknown questions and escalates to human agents, the resolved answers remain locked in ticket archives without updating the AI's knowledge base.
solution: Autonomous escalation FSM where human agent resolutions are deterministically upserted into ChromaDB under deterministic keys (learned-{id}) in real-time.
metrics: Instant knowledge base updating upon agent resolution
tradeoff: Real-Time Closed-Loop Ingestion vs Costly, delayed fine-tuning cycles with static models

title: Offline-First Data Sync with Dexie.js (IndexedDB) for Unreliable Networks
dilemma: Weak and intermittent classroom internet connectivity causing data loss and blocking teachers during memorization logging.
solution: Offline-first architecture storing operational logs in client-side IndexedDB via Dexie.js, with bidirectional background reconciliation to Django REST APIs on reconnect.
metrics: 300+ students tracked with zero network-induced data loss
tradeoff: Client IndexedDB + Background Sync vs Cloud-only synchronous requests failing offline

title: Process Lifecycle Management, Pipes & Signal Handling in C
dilemma: Building an in-depth Unix shell in C handling fork/exec pipelines, background jobs, and signal propagation without creating zombie processes or memory leaks.
solution: Strict POSIX process management: fork/execvp with dup2 descriptor redirection, pipe chaining, SIGCHLD asynchronous zombie process reaping, and terminal signal handling.
metrics: Zero zombie processes, robust pipeline execution
tradeoff: POSIX system calls + Async SIGCHLD reaping vs Blocking waitpid or unhandled child processes
